In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis, pharmacological activity and molecular docking of a series of novel ureidophosphonic acids.
the synthesis and evaluation of the anticholinesterasic (AChE inhibitory activity) of some 1-ureidoalkylphosphonates, as well as with the investigation of their molecular docking with the enzyme.
the design and synthesis of 1-substituted ureidophosphonic acid derivatives, which have been tested for their inhibitory activity on AChE.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ureidophosphates 3i and 3j are the most potent compounds in this study.
the synthesized compounds are promising candidates for AChE inhibitor.
1-ureido-3-phenyl-3-oxopropane-1,1,3-triphosphonic acid diethyl ester (compound 3j) is the best inhibitor for the enzyme AChEs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the 1-ureido group is an important structural element that could be used to design new potent AChE inhibitors.
the ureidophosphonic acid derivatives are promising AChE inhibitors and could be used as lead compounds in the design of new and more potent AChE inhibitors.
1-ureidoalkyl phosphonates could be used as a new type of AChE inhibitor with a high selectivity toward the PAS site.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ureidophosphonic acid derivatives could be a good lead for the design of new AChE inhibitor.
the 1-ureido-2-(3,4,5-trimethoxybenzoyl)-phosphonates (3a, b, and c) are more potent inhibitors of AChE than the 1-phenyl-2-(3',4',5'-trimethoxybenzamido)-phosphonate (1a).
it is possible to develop new AChE inhibitors by modifying the structure of the parent molecule, in our case the phosphonate, by the introduction of ureidogroup.
